+"""Derive the higher-timeframe edge side from completed daily closes."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+
+import pandas as pd
+
+from app.core.enums import Side, Timeframe
+
+
+def edge_side(
+    frames: Mapping[Timeframe, pd.DataFrame], at: pd.Timestamp, entry: Timeframe
+) -> Side | None:
+    """Return the D1 side above ``entry``; no clear D1 edge means no trade.
+
+    The lane's H1 index is close-stamped, so it is shifted to the bar open before UTC-day resampling.
+    Only completed daily bars are used. A rising 50-day simple mean needs two full windows (51 closes);
+    a shorter history or a mixed/flat regime returns ``None``. This is the owner's hard rule, not a
+    configurable fallback: no clear edge side above the entry frame means no trade.
+    """
+    if entry.seconds >= Timeframe.D1.seconds:
+        raise ValueError("entry timeframe must be smaller than D1")
+
+    h1 = frames.get(Timeframe.H1)
+    if h1 is None or len(h1) < 1200 or "close" not in h1:
+        return None
+
+    opens = h1.copy()
+    opens.index = pd.DatetimeIndex(opens.index) - pd.Timedelta(hours=1)
+    daily = opens.resample("1D").agg({"close": "last"}).dropna()
+    closed = daily[(daily.index + pd.Timedelta(days=1)) <= pd.Timestamp(at)]
+    if len(closed) < 51:
+        return None
+
+    means = closed.close.rolling(window=50, min_periods=50).mean()
+    current_close = float(closed.close.iloc[-1])
+    current_mean = float(means.iloc[-1])
+    previous_mean = float(means.iloc[-2])
+    if current_close > current_mean and current_mean > previous_mean:
+        return Side.BUY
+    if current_close < current_mean and current_mean < previous_mean:
+        return Side.SELL
+    return None

+"""A validated, inert vessel for research-supplied weighted trade readings."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Literal
+
+Wants = Literal["high", "low", "true", "false"]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Weight:
+    """A reading and the nonnegative amount it contributes to a weighted decision."""
+
+    name: str
+    weight: float
+    wants: Wants
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not self.name:
+            raise ValueError("weight name must not be empty")
+        if not math.isfinite(self.weight) or self.weight < 0:
+            raise ValueError("weight must be finite and >= 0")
+        if self.wants not in ("high", "low", "true", "false"):
+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported wants value: {self.wants!r}")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Scale:
+    """The readings and minimum normalized score required to qualify."""
+
+    weights: tuple[Weight, ...]
+    threshold: float
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not math.isfinite(self.threshold) or not 0 <= self.threshold <= 1:
+            raise ValueError("threshold must be finite and in [0, 1]")
+        names = [reading.name for reading in self.weights]
+        if len(names) != len(set(names)):
+            raise ValueError("weight names must be unique")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ScoreResult:
+    """Normalized score, per-reading classifications, and threshold outcome."""
+
+    score: float
+    supported: list[str]
+    opposed: list[str]
+    missing: list[str]
+    meets_threshold: bool
+
+
+def score(readings: Mapping[str, float | bool | None], scale: Scale) -> ScoreResult:
+    """Score available readings over their readable weight only.
+
+    Numeric values must already be normalized to ``[0, 1]`` by the caller. ``high`` earns
+    ``weight * value`` and ``low`` earns ``weight * (1 - value)``; a numeric reading supports when
+    its contribution is at least half its weight, otherwise it opposes. Boolean readings earn full
+    weight only when their value matches ``true`` or ``false``. Missing values are excluded from
+    both numerator and denominator. The threshold is met at ``score >= threshold``; an empty or
+    zero-readable-weight scale cannot meet it.
+    """
+    numerator = 0.0
+    denominator = 0.0
+    supported: list[str] = []
+    opposed: list[str] = []
+    missing: list[str] = []
+
+    for item in scale.weights:
+        value = readings.get(item.name)
+        if value is None:
+            missing.append(item.name)
+            continue
+
+        if isinstance(value, bool):
+            if item.wants not in ("true", "false"):
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: boolean reading requires wants='true' or 'false'")
+            agrees = value is (item.wants == "true")
+            contribution = item.weight if agrees else 0.0
+            if agrees:
+                supported.append(item.name)
+            else:
+                opposed.append(item.name)
+        else:
+            if item.wants not in ("high", "low"):
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: numeric reading requires wants='high' or 'low'")
+            numeric = float(value)
+            if not math.isfinite(numeric) or not 0 <= numeric <= 1:
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: numeric reading must be finite and in [0, 1]")
+            fraction = numeric if item.wants == "high" else 1.0 - numeric
+            contribution = item.weight * fraction
+            (supported if fraction >= 0.5 else opposed).append(item.name)
+        numerator += contribution
+        denominator += item.weight
+
+    total = numerator / denominator if denominator > 0 else 0.0
+    meets = denominator > 0 and total >= scale.threshold
+    return ScoreResult(total, supported, opposed, missing, meets)

+def restore_any() -> None:
+    """Recover any source files parked before an interrupted mutation run."""
+    if not BACKUP.exists():
+        return
+    for parked in sorted(BACKUP.glob("*.bak")):
+        relative = parked.stem.replace("__", "/")
+        (ROOT / relative).write_bytes(parked.read_bytes())
+        parked.unlink()
+        sys.stdout.write(f"restored {relative} from an interrupted run\n")
+    if not any(BACKUP.iterdir()):
+        BACKUP.rmdir()
+
+
+def run_test(test: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
+    return subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed interpreter and repository-owned test selectors
+        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", f"tests/unit/{test}"],
+        cwd=ROOT,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=False,
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    restore_any()
+    test_paths = sorted({bug.test.split("::", 1)[0] for bug in BUGS})
+    baseline = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed interpreter and repository-owned test paths
+        [
+            sys.executable,
+            "-m",
+            "pytest",
+            "-q",
+            "-p",
+            "no:cacheprovider",
+            *[f"tests/unit/{p}" for p in test_paths],
+        ],
+        cwd=ROOT,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=False,
+    )
+    if baseline.returncode:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"focused baseline tests failed:\n{baseline.stdout}\n{baseline.stderr}")
+
+    BACKUP.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    clean_files: dict[str, bytes] = {}
+    results: list[str] = []
+    try:
+        for bug in BUGS:
+            target = ROOT / bug.path
+            clean = clean_files.setdefault(bug.path, target.read_bytes())
+            parked = BACKUP / (bug.path.replace("/", "__") + ".bak")
+            if not parked.exists():
+                parked.write_bytes(clean)
+            current = target.read_bytes()
+            if current.count(bug.old) != 1 or bug.old == bug.new:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"mutation anchor is not unique for: {bug.name}")
+            try:
+                target.write_bytes(current.replace(bug.old, bug.new, 1))
+                outcome = run_test(bug.test)
+                caught = outcome.returncode != 0
+                results.append(f"{'CAUGHT' if caught else 'MISSED'} | {bug.test} | {bug.name}")
+                if not caught:
+                    results.append(outcome.stdout.strip() or "mutation test exited successfully")
+            finally:
+                target.write_bytes(clean)
+
+        caught_count = sum(row.startswith("CAUGHT") for row in results)
+        output = "\n".join([*results, f"{caught_count}/{len(BUGS)} caught"]) + "\n"
+        (HERE / "plant_bugs_3_output.txt").write_text(output, encoding="utf-8")
+        sys.stdout.write(output)
+        return 0 if caught_count == len(BUGS) else 1
+    finally:
+        for relative, original in clean_files.items():
+            target = ROOT / relative
+            target.write_bytes(original)
+            parked = BACKUP / (relative.replace("/", "__") + ".bak")
+            if parked.exists() and parked.read_bytes() != original:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"backup mismatch while restoring {relative}")
+            parked.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+        if BACKUP.exists() and not any(BACKUP.iterdir()):
+            BACKUP.rmdir()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+"""Hand-worked D1 edge-side cases derived from close-stamped H1 candles."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
+
+import pandas as pd
+import pytest
+
+from app.core.enums import Side, Timeframe
+from app.strategy.edge_side import edge_side
+
+
+def daily_context(closes: list[float], *, partial_close: float | None = None):
+    start = datetime(2026, 1, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
+    index = pd.date_range(start=start, periods=len(closes) * 24, freq="1h")
+    hourly_closes = [value for value in closes for _ in range(24)]
+    frame = pd.DataFrame({"close": hourly_closes}, index=index)
+    if partial_close is not None:
+        partial_index = pd.date_range(index[-1] + timedelta(hours=1), periods=23, freq="1h")
+        frame = pd.concat([frame, pd.DataFrame({"close": partial_close}, index=partial_index)])
+    at = pd.Timestamp(frame.index[-1])
+    return {Timeframe.H1: frame}, at
+
+
+def test_rising_daily_mean_with_close_above_it_is_buy():
+    # The last two 50-close means are 124.5 and 125.5; close 150 is above the rising mean.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.BUY
+
+
+def test_falling_daily_mean_with_close_below_it_is_sell():
+    # The last two 50-close means are 175.5 and 174.5; close 150 is below the falling mean.
+    frames, at = daily_context([200.0 - day for day in range(51)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.SELL
+
+
+def test_close_above_a_falling_mean_is_mixed():
+    # The current mean falls from 175.5 to 175.3, while close 190 stays above it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([200.0 - day for day in range(50)] + [190.0])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_close_below_a_rising_mean_is_mixed():
+    # The current mean rises from 124.5 to 124.9, while close 120 stays below it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)] + [120.0])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_exactly_fifty_closed_daily_bars_do_not_guess_the_mean_slope():
+    # Fifty closes form one 50-day mean, but there is no prior full-window mean to compare with it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_forty_nine_closed_daily_bars_return_no_side():
+    # Moving the cutoff back one day leaves exactly 49 complete daily bins from these 1,200 H1 rows.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)])
+    at -= pd.Timedelta(days=1)
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_unclosed_daily_bar_does_not_change_the_edge_side():
+    # The 51st full close is 150 with means 175.5 -> 174.5; a forming 500 close would reverse the regime.
+    closes = [200.0 - day for day in range(51)]
+    frames, at = daily_context(closes, partial_close=500.0)
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.SELL
+
+
+def test_entry_at_or_above_daily_raises_value_error():
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="smaller than D1"):
+        edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.D1)
+
+
+def test_short_h1_history_returns_no_side():
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    frame = frames[Timeframe.H1].drop(frames[Timeframe.H1].index[10:35])
+    frames = {Timeframe.H1: frame}
+    assert len(frame) < 1200
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None

+"""Hand-worked weighted-score cases; every expected score is calculated in the test comments."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+
+from app.strategy.weighing import Scale, Weight, score
+
+
+def test_all_readings_agree():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("a", 2.0, "true"), Weight("b", 1.0, "high")), 1.0)
+    got = score({"a": True, "b": 1.0}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 1.0  # (2 + 1) / (2 + 1)
+    assert got.supported == ["a", "b"]
+    assert got.opposed == [] and got.missing == [] and got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_all_readings_disagree():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("a", 2.0, "true"), Weight("b", 1.0, "high")), 0.5)
+    got = score({"a": False, "b": 0.0}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 0.0  # (0 + 0) / 3
+    assert got.supported == [] and got.opposed == ["a", "b"]
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_mixed_readings_use_weighted_contributions():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("yes", 2.0, "true"), Weight("trend", 3.0, "high")), 0.5)
+    got = score({"yes": True, "trend": 0.4}, scale)
+    assert got.score == pytest.approx(3.2 / 5.0)  # (2 + 3 * .4) / 5
+    assert got.supported == ["yes"] and got.opposed == ["trend"]
+    assert got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_missing_reading_is_removed_from_the_denominator():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("yes", 1.0, "true"), Weight("absent", 3.0, "true")), 0.9)
+    got = score({"yes": True}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 1.0  # 1 / 1, not 1 / 4
+    assert got.supported == ["yes"] and got.missing == ["absent"]
+    assert got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_low_numeric_reading_scores_the_complement():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("noise", 4.0, "low"),), 0.5)
+    got = score({"noise": 0.25}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 0.75  # 4 * (1 - .25) / 4
+    assert got.supported == ["noise"] and got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_empty_scale_scores_zero_and_has_no_readings():
+    got = score({}, Scale((), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0
+    assert got.supported == [] and got.opposed == [] and got.missing == []
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_zero_weight_is_readable_but_cannot_create_a_score():
+    got = score({"signal": True}, Scale((Weight("signal", 0.0, "true"),), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0
+    assert got.supported == ["signal"] and got.opposed == []
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_threshold_is_met_at_equality():
+    got = score({"signal": 0.75}, Scale((Weight("signal", 2.0, "high"),), 0.75))
+    assert got.score == 0.75  # (2 * .75) / 2
+    assert got.meets_threshold  # The documented comparison is >=.
+
+
+def test_none_is_reported_as_missing():
+    got = score({"signal": None}, Scale((Weight("signal", 1.0, "true"),), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0 and got.missing == ["signal"]
+    assert got.supported == [] and got.opposed == [] and not got.meets_threshold

def pinned_config() -> Path:
    """The repository's config.yaml with :data:`PINNED_RISK`, in a temporary file."""
    raw = yaml.safe_load(Path("config.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    raw["risk"] |= PINNED_RISK
    path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="taa-samples-")) / "config.yaml"
    path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(raw, sort_keys=False), encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return path

+"""Derive the higher-timeframe edge side from completed daily closes."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+
+import pandas as pd
+
+from app.core.enums import Side, Timeframe
+
+
+def edge_side(
+    frames: Mapping[Timeframe, pd.DataFrame], at: pd.Timestamp, entry: Timeframe
+) -> Side | None:
+    """Return the D1 side above ``entry``; no clear D1 edge means no trade.
+
+    The lane's H1 index is close-stamped, so it is shifted to the bar open before UTC-day resampling.
+    Only completed daily bars are used. A rising 50-day simple mean needs two full windows (51 closes);
+    a shorter history or a mixed/flat regime returns ``None``. This is the owner's hard rule, not a
+    configurable fallback: no clear edge side above the entry frame means no trade.
+    """
+    if entry.seconds >= Timeframe.D1.seconds:
+        raise ValueError("entry timeframe must be smaller than D1")
+
+    h1 = frames.get(Timeframe.H1)
+    if h1 is None or len(h1) < 1200 or "close" not in h1:
+        return None
+
+    opens = h1.copy()
+    opens.index = pd.DatetimeIndex(opens.index) - pd.Timedelta(hours=1)
+    daily = opens.resample("1D").agg({"close": "last"}).dropna()
+    closed = daily[(daily.index + pd.Timedelta(days=1)) <= pd.Timestamp(at)]
+    if len(closed) < 51:
+        return None
+
+    means = closed.close.rolling(window=50, min_periods=50).mean()
+    current_close = float(closed.close.iloc[-1])
+    current_mean = float(means.iloc[-1])
+    previous_mean = float(means.iloc[-2])
+    if current_close > current_mean and current_mean > previous_mean:
+        return Side.BUY
+    if current_close < current_mean and current_mean < previous_mean:
+        return Side.SELL
+    return None

+"""A validated, inert vessel for research-supplied weighted trade readings."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Literal
+
+Wants = Literal["high", "low", "true", "false"]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Weight:
+    """A reading and the nonnegative amount it contributes to a weighted decision."""
+
+    name: str
+    weight: float
+    wants: Wants
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not self.name:
+            raise ValueError("weight name must not be empty")
+        if not math.isfinite(self.weight) or self.weight < 0:
+            raise ValueError("weight must be finite and >= 0")
+        if self.wants not in ("high", "low", "true", "false"):
+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported wants value: {self.wants!r}")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Scale:
+    """The readings and minimum normalized score required to qualify."""
+
+    weights: tuple[Weight, ...]
+    threshold: float
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not math.isfinite(self.threshold) or not 0 <= self.threshold <= 1:
+            raise ValueError("threshold must be finite and in [0, 1]")
+        names = [reading.name for reading in self.weights]
+        if len(names) != len(set(names)):
+            raise ValueError("weight names must be unique")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ScoreResult:
+    """Normalized score, per-reading classifications, and threshold outcome."""
+
+    score: float
+    supported: list[str]
+    opposed: list[str]
+    missing: list[str]
+    meets_threshold: bool
+
+
+def score(readings: Mapping[str, float | bool | None], scale: Scale) -> ScoreResult:
+    """Score available readings over their readable weight only.
+
+    Numeric values must already be normalized to ``[0, 1]`` by the caller. ``high`` earns
+    ``weight * value`` and ``low`` earns ``weight * (1 - value)``; a numeric reading supports when
+    its contribution is at least half its weight, otherwise it opposes. Boolean readings earn full
+    weight only when their value matches ``true`` or ``false``. Missing values are excluded from
+    both numerator and denominator. The threshold is met at ``score >= threshold``; an empty or
+    zero-readable-weight scale cannot meet it.
+    """
+    numerator = 0.0
+    denominator = 0.0
+    supported: list[str] = []
+    opposed: list[str] = []
+    missing: list[str] = []
+
+    for item in scale.weights:
+        value = readings.get(item.name)
+        if value is None:
+            missing.append(item.name)
+            continue
+
+        if isinstance(value, bool):
+            if item.wants not in ("true", "false"):
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: boolean reading requires wants='true' or 'false'")
+            agrees = value is (item.wants == "true")
+            contribution = item.weight if agrees else 0.0
+            if agrees:
+                supported.append(item.name)
+            else:
+                opposed.append(item.name)
+        else:
+            if item.wants not in ("high", "low"):
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: numeric reading requires wants='high' or 'low'")
+            numeric = float(value)
+            if not math.isfinite(numeric) or not 0 <= numeric <= 1:
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: numeric reading must be finite and in [0, 1]")
+            fraction = numeric if item.wants == "high" else 1.0 - numeric
+            contribution = item.weight * fraction
+            (supported if fraction >= 0.5 else opposed).append(item.name)
+        numerator += contribution
+        denominator += item.weight
+
+    total = numerator / denominator if denominator > 0 else 0.0
+    meets = denominator > 0 and total >= scale.threshold
+    return ScoreResult(total, supported, opposed, missing, meets)

+# DEV_NOTES_3
+
+Date: 2026-10-27
+
+## Tasks A–C
+
+- **A — `edge_side.py`:** Added a pure D1 regime reader from close-stamped H1 candles. It shifts the index back one hour, resamples daily closes, filters daily bars closed at `at`, and returns BUY/SELL only when close and the 50-day SMA slope agree. It rejects entry frames at or above D1 and returns `None` for missing/short data, mixed readings, and an incomplete D1 bar.
+- **B — trend and range bots:** Added `require_edge_side=False` to both parameter models. The trend bots check it immediately after their session window and before reading other decision data; enabling it requests 1,200 H1 warmup bars. The range bot checks the break side against the D1 side after finding a break. A missing edge side holds every enabled bot with `AGAINST_EDGE_SIDE`. Default behavior remains off. The shared API sample fixture now records the two new `false` defaults.
+- **C — `weighing.py`:** Added immutable `Weight` and `Scale` models and `score()`. Missing readings leave both parts of the ratio; numeric inputs are validated in `[0, 1]` and are not normalized by this module. The normalized score is weighted contribution / available weight. Boolean support means the value matches `wants`; numeric support means the contribution fraction is at least 0.5. `meets_threshold` uses `>=`; empty and zero-readable-weight scales do not meet even a zero threshold. No strategy calls the scorer yet.
+
+## Tests and mutation proof
+
+There are 26 new test cases. Each case was run against a targeted one-line production mutation; the default-off test has separate mutations for the trend and range parameter defaults. The 25 planted mutations caught all 25 cases. Full details are in [plant_bugs_3_output.txt](plant_bugs_3_output.txt).

+## Clarity and interpretation
+
+No instructions conflict. Two details needed explicit definitions:
+
+1. Exactly 50 closed daily closes produce one 50-day mean, but cannot establish whether that mean is rising or falling without a prior full 50-day window. I fail closed with `None` at 50 and classify only once 51 closes are available. This is covered by the 50-bar and 49-bar boundary tests.
+2. The spec asks for supported/opposed lists for continuous numeric readings but does not define their dividing line. I classify the normalized contribution fraction at or above 0.5 as support and below 0.5 as opposition, documented in `score()`.

+def restore_any() -> None:
+    """Recover any source files parked before an interrupted mutation run."""
+    if not BACKUP.exists():
+        return
+    for parked in sorted(BACKUP.glob("*.bak")):
+        relative = parked.stem.replace("__", "/")
+        (ROOT / relative).write_bytes(parked.read_bytes())
+        parked.unlink()
+        sys.stdout.write(f"restored {relative} from an interrupted run\n")
+    if not any(BACKUP.iterdir()):
+        BACKUP.rmdir()
+
+
+def run_test(test: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
+    return subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed interpreter and repository-owned test selectors
+        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", f"tests/unit/{test}"],
+        cwd=ROOT,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=False,
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    restore_any()
+    test_paths = sorted({bug.test.split("::", 1)[0] for bug in BUGS})
+    baseline = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed interpreter and repository-owned test paths
+        [
+            sys.executable,
+            "-m",
+            "pytest",
+            "-q",
+            "-p",
+            "no:cacheprovider",
+            *[f"tests/unit/{p}" for p in test_paths],
+        ],
+        cwd=ROOT,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=False,
+    )
+    if baseline.returncode:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"focused baseline tests failed:\n{baseline.stdout}\n{baseline.stderr}")
+
+    BACKUP.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    clean_files: dict[str, bytes] = {}
+    results: list[str] = []
+    try:
+        for bug in BUGS:
+            target = ROOT / bug.path
+            clean = clean_files.setdefault(bug.path, target.read_bytes())
+            parked = BACKUP / (bug.path.replace("/", "__") + ".bak")
+            if not parked.exists():
+                parked.write_bytes(clean)
+            current = target.read_bytes()
+            if current.count(bug.old) != 1 or bug.old == bug.new:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"mutation anchor is not unique for: {bug.name}")
+            try:
+                target.write_bytes(current.replace(bug.old, bug.new, 1))
+                outcome = run_test(bug.test)
+                caught = outcome.returncode != 0
+                results.append(f"{'CAUGHT' if caught else 'MISSED'} | {bug.test} | {bug.name}")
+                if not caught:
+                    results.append(outcome.stdout.strip() or "mutation test exited successfully")
+            finally:
+                target.write_bytes(clean)
+
+        caught_count = sum(row.startswith("CAUGHT") for row in results)
+        output = "\n".join([*results, f"{caught_count}/{len(BUGS)} caught"]) + "\n"
+        (HERE / "plant_bugs_3_output.txt").write_text(output, encoding="utf-8")
+        sys.stdout.write(output)
+        return 0 if caught_count == len(BUGS) else 1
+    finally:
+        for relative, original in clean_files.items():
+            target = ROOT / relative
+            target.write_bytes(original)
+            parked = BACKUP / (relative.replace("/", "__") + ".bak")
+            if parked.exists() and parked.read_bytes() != original:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"backup mismatch while restoring {relative}")
+            parked.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+        if BACKUP.exists() and not any(BACKUP.iterdir()):
+            BACKUP.rmdir()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+"""Hand-worked D1 edge-side cases derived from close-stamped H1 candles."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
+
+import pandas as pd
+import pytest
+
+from app.core.enums import Side, Timeframe
+from app.strategy.edge_side import edge_side
+
+
+def daily_context(closes: list[float], *, partial_close: float | None = None):
+    start = datetime(2026, 1, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
+    index = pd.date_range(start=start, periods=len(closes) * 24, freq="1h")
+    hourly_closes = [value for value in closes for _ in range(24)]
+    frame = pd.DataFrame({"close": hourly_closes}, index=index)
+    if partial_close is not None:
+        partial_index = pd.date_range(index[-1] + timedelta(hours=1), periods=23, freq="1h")
+        frame = pd.concat([frame, pd.DataFrame({"close": partial_close}, index=partial_index)])
+    at = pd.Timestamp(frame.index[-1])
+    return {Timeframe.H1: frame}, at
+
+
+def test_rising_daily_mean_with_close_above_it_is_buy():
+    # The last two 50-close means are 124.5 and 125.5; close 150 is above the rising mean.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.BUY
+
+
+def test_falling_daily_mean_with_close_below_it_is_sell():
+    # The last two 50-close means are 175.5 and 174.5; close 150 is below the falling mean.
+    frames, at = daily_context([200.0 - day for day in range(51)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.SELL
+
+
+def test_close_above_a_falling_mean_is_mixed():
+    # The current mean falls from 175.5 to 175.3, while close 190 stays above it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([200.0 - day for day in range(50)] + [190.0])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_close_below_a_rising_mean_is_mixed():
+    # The current mean rises from 124.5 to 124.9, while close 120 stays below it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)] + [120.0])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_exactly_fifty_closed_daily_bars_do_not_guess_the_mean_slope():
+    # Fifty closes form one 50-day mean, but there is no prior full-window mean to compare with it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_forty_nine_closed_daily_bars_return_no_side():
+    # Moving the cutoff back one day leaves exactly 49 complete daily bins from these 1,200 H1 rows.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)])
+    at -= pd.Timedelta(days=1)
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_unclosed_daily_bar_does_not_change_the_edge_side():
+    # The 51st full close is 150 with means 175.5 -> 174.5; a forming 500 close would reverse the regime.
+    closes = [200.0 - day for day in range(51)]
+    frames, at = daily_context(closes, partial_close=500.0)
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.SELL
+
+
+def test_entry_at_or_above_daily_raises_value_error():
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="smaller than D1"):
+        edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.D1)
+
+
+def test_short_h1_history_returns_no_side():
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    frame = frames[Timeframe.H1].drop(frames[Timeframe.H1].index[10:35])
+    frames = {Timeframe.H1: frame}
+    assert len(frame) < 1200
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None

+"""Hand-worked weighted-score cases; every expected score is calculated in the test comments."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+
+from app.strategy.weighing import Scale, Weight, score
+
+
+def test_all_readings_agree():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("a", 2.0, "true"), Weight("b", 1.0, "high")), 1.0)
+    got = score({"a": True, "b": 1.0}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 1.0  # (2 + 1) / (2 + 1)
+    assert got.supported == ["a", "b"]
+    assert got.opposed == [] and got.missing == [] and got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_all_readings_disagree():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("a", 2.0, "true"), Weight("b", 1.0, "high")), 0.5)
+    got = score({"a": False, "b": 0.0}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 0.0  # (0 + 0) / 3
+    assert got.supported == [] and got.opposed == ["a", "b"]
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_mixed_readings_use_weighted_contributions():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("yes", 2.0, "true"), Weight("trend", 3.0, "high")), 0.5)
+    got = score({"yes": True, "trend": 0.4}, scale)
+    assert got.score == pytest.approx(3.2 / 5.0)  # (2 + 3 * .4) / 5
+    assert got.supported == ["yes"] and got.opposed == ["trend"]
+    assert got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_missing_reading_is_removed_from_the_denominator():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("yes", 1.0, "true"), Weight("absent", 3.0, "true")), 0.9)
+    got = score({"yes": True}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 1.0  # 1 / 1, not 1 / 4
+    assert got.supported == ["yes"] and got.missing == ["absent"]
+    assert got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_low_numeric_reading_scores_the_complement():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("noise", 4.0, "low"),), 0.5)
+    got = score({"noise": 0.25}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 0.75  # 4 * (1 - .25) / 4
+    assert got.supported == ["noise"] and got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_empty_scale_scores_zero_and_has_no_readings():
+    got = score({}, Scale((), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0
+    assert got.supported == [] and got.opposed == [] and got.missing == []
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_zero_weight_is_readable_but_cannot_create_a_score():
+    got = score({"signal": True}, Scale((Weight("signal", 0.0, "true"),), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0
+    assert got.supported == ["signal"] and got.opposed == []
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_threshold_is_met_at_equality():
+    got = score({"signal": 0.75}, Scale((Weight("signal", 2.0, "high"),), 0.75))
+    assert got.score == 0.75  # (2 * .75) / 2
+    assert got.meets_threshold  # The documented comparison is >=.
+
+
+def test_none_is_reported_as_missing():
+    got = score({"signal": None}, Scale((Weight("signal", 1.0, "true"),), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0 and got.missing == ["signal"]

+"""Derive the higher-timeframe edge side from completed daily closes."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+
+import pandas as pd
+
+from app.core.enums import Side, Timeframe
+
+
+def edge_side(
+    frames: Mapping[Timeframe, pd.DataFrame], at: pd.Timestamp, entry: Timeframe
+) -> Side | None:
+    """Return the D1 side above ``entry``; no clear D1 edge means no trade.
+
+    The lane's H1 index is close-stamped, so it is shifted to the bar open before UTC-day resampling.
+    Only completed daily bars are used. A rising 50-day simple mean needs two full windows (51 closes);
+    a shorter history or a mixed/flat regime returns ``None``. This is the owner's hard rule, not a
+    configurable fallback: no clear edge side above the entry frame means no trade.
+    """
+    if entry.seconds >= Timeframe.D1.seconds:
+        raise ValueError("entry timeframe must be smaller than D1")
+
+    h1 = frames.get(Timeframe.H1)
+    if h1 is None or len(h1) < 1200 or "close" not in h1:
+        return None
+
+    opens = h1.copy()
+    opens.index = pd.DatetimeIndex(opens.index) - pd.Timedelta(hours=1)
+    daily = opens.resample("1D").agg({"close": "last"}).dropna()
+    closed = daily[(daily.index + pd.Timedelta(days=1)) <= pd.Timestamp(at)]
+    if len(closed) < 51:
+        return None
+
+    means = closed.close.rolling(window=50, min_periods=50).mean()
+    current_close = float(closed.close.iloc[-1])
+    current_mean = float(means.iloc[-1])
+    previous_mean = float(means.iloc[-2])
+    if current_close > current_mean and current_mean > previous_mean:
+        return Side.BUY
+    if current_close < current_mean and current_mean < previous_mean:
+        return Side.SELL
+    return None

+"""A validated, inert vessel for research-supplied weighted trade readings."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Literal
+
+Wants = Literal["high", "low", "true", "false"]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Weight:
+    """A reading and the nonnegative amount it contributes to a weighted decision."""
+
+    name: str
+    weight: float
+    wants: Wants
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not self.name:
+            raise ValueError("weight name must not be empty")
+        if not math.isfinite(self.weight) or self.weight < 0:
+            raise ValueError("weight must be finite and >= 0")
+        if self.wants not in ("high", "low", "true", "false"):
+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported wants value: {self.wants!r}")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Scale:
+    """The readings and minimum normalized score required to qualify."""
+
+    weights: tuple[Weight, ...]
+    threshold: float
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not math.isfinite(self.threshold) or not 0 <= self.threshold <= 1:
+            raise ValueError("threshold must be finite and in [0, 1]")
+        names = [reading.name for reading in self.weights]
+        if len(names) != len(set(names)):
+            raise ValueError("weight names must be unique")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ScoreResult:
+    """Normalized score, per-reading classifications, and threshold outcome."""
+
+    score: float
+    supported: list[str]
+    opposed: list[str]
+    missing: list[str]
+    meets_threshold: bool
+
+
+def score(readings: Mapping[str, float | bool | None], scale: Scale) -> ScoreResult:
+    """Score available readings over their readable weight only.
+
+    Numeric values must already be normalized to ``[0, 1]`` by the caller. ``high`` earns
+    ``weight * value`` and ``low`` earns ``weight * (1 - value)``; a numeric reading supports when
+    its contribution is at least half its weight, otherwise it opposes. Boolean readings earn full
+    weight only when their value matches ``true`` or ``false``. Missing values are excluded from
+    both numerator and denominator. The threshold is met at ``score >= threshold``; an empty or
+    zero-readable-weight scale cannot meet it.
+    """
+    numerator = 0.0
+    denominator = 0.0
+    supported: list[str] = []
+    opposed: list[str] = []
+    missing: list[str] = []
+
+    for item in scale.weights:
+        value = readings.get(item.name)
+        if value is None:
+            missing.append(item.name)
+            continue
+
+        if isinstance(value, bool):
+            if item.wants not in ("true", "false"):
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: boolean reading requires wants='true' or 'false'")
+            agrees = value is (item.wants == "true")
+            contribution = item.weight if agrees else 0.0
+            if agrees:
+                supported.append(item.name)
+            else:
+                opposed.append(item.name)
+        else:
+            if item.wants not in ("high", "low"):
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: numeric reading requires wants='high' or 'low'")
+            numeric = float(value)
+            if not math.isfinite(numeric) or not 0 <= numeric <= 1:
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: numeric reading must be finite and in [0, 1]")
+            fraction = numeric if item.wants == "high" else 1.0 - numeric
+            contribution = item.weight * fraction
+            (supported if fraction >= 0.5 else opposed).append(item.name)
+        numerator += contribution
+        denominator += item.weight
+
+    total = numerator / denominator if denominator > 0 else 0.0
+    meets = denominator > 0 and total >= scale.threshold
+    return ScoreResult(total, supported, opposed, missing, meets)

+# DEV_NOTES_3
+
+Date: 2026-10-27
+
+## Tasks A–C
+
+- **A — `edge_side.py`:** Added a pure D1 regime reader from close-stamped H1 candles. It shifts the index back one hour, resamples daily closes, filters daily bars closed at `at`, and returns BUY/SELL only when close and the 50-day SMA slope agree. It rejects entry frames at or above D1 and returns `None` for missing/short data, mixed readings, and an incomplete D1 bar.
+- **B — trend and range bots:** Added `require_edge_side=False` to both parameter models. The trend bots check it immediately after their session window and before reading other decision data; enabling it requests 1,200 H1 warmup bars. The range bot checks the break side against the D1 side after finding a break. A missing edge side holds every enabled bot with `AGAINST_EDGE_SIDE`. Default behavior remains off. The shared API sample fixture now records the two new `false` defaults.
+- **C — `weighing.py`:** Added immutable `Weight` and `Scale` models and `score()`. Missing readings leave both parts of the ratio; numeric inputs are validated in `[0, 1]` and are not normalized by this module. The normalized score is weighted contribution / available weight. Boolean support means the value matches `wants`; numeric support means the contribution fraction is at least 0.5. `meets_threshold` uses `>=`; empty and zero-readable-weight scales do not meet even a zero threshold. No strategy calls the scorer yet.
+

+
+There are 26 new test cases. Each case was run against a targeted one-line production mutation; the default-off test has separate mutations for the trend and range parameter defaults. The 25 planted mutations caught all 25 cases. Full details are in [plant_bugs_3_output.txt](plant_bugs_3_output.txt).

+## Clarity and interpretation
+
+No instructions conflict. Two details needed explicit definitions:
+
+1. Exactly 50 closed daily closes produce one 50-day mean, but cannot establish whether that mean is rising or falling without a prior full 50-day window. I fail closed with `None` at 50 and classify only once 51 closes are available. This is covered by the 50-bar and 49-bar boundary tests.
+2. The spec asks for supported/opposed lists for continuous numeric readings but does not define their dividing line. I classify the normalized contribution fraction at or above 0.5 as support and below 0.5 as opposition, documented in `score()`.
+
+The owner’s rule says it applies to the AI trader too, while Task B specifies only `trend_box_down`, `trend_box_up`, and `range_break`, with a new opt-in parameter on those classes. I applied Task B to its three named strategies and did not add an AI-trader gate because no AI parameter or gate ordering is specified. The AI path therefore remains outside this implementation and needs an explicit follow-up decision to fulfill the wider statement.

+def restore_any() -> None:
+    """Recover any source files parked before an interrupted mutation run."""
+    if not BACKUP.exists():
+        return
+    for parked in sorted(BACKUP.glob("*.bak")):
+        relative = parked.stem.replace("__", "/")
+        (ROOT / relative).write_bytes(parked.read_bytes())
+        parked.unlink()
+        sys.stdout.write(f"restored {relative} from an interrupted run\n")
+    if not any(BACKUP.iterdir()):
+        BACKUP.rmdir()
+
+
+def run_test(test: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
+    return subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed interpreter and repository-owned test selectors
+        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", f"tests/unit/{test}"],
+        cwd=ROOT,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=False,
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    restore_any()
+    test_paths = sorted({bug.test.split("::", 1)[0] for bug in BUGS})
+    baseline = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed interpreter and repository-owned test paths
+        [
+            sys.executable,
+            "-m",
+            "pytest",
+            "-q",
+            "-p",
+            "no:cacheprovider",
+            *[f"tests/unit/{p}" for p in test_paths],
+        ],
+        cwd=ROOT,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=False,
+    )
+    if baseline.returncode:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"focused baseline tests failed:\n{baseline.stdout}\n{baseline.stderr}")
+
+    BACKUP.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    clean_files: dict[str, bytes] = {}
+    results: list[str] = []
+    try:
+        for bug in BUGS:
+            target = ROOT / bug.path
+            clean = clean_files.setdefault(bug.path, target.read_bytes())
+            parked = BACKUP / (bug.path.replace("/", "__") + ".bak")
+            if not parked.exists():
+                parked.write_bytes(clean)
+            current = target.read_bytes()
+            if current.count(bug.old) != 1 or bug.old == bug.new:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"mutation anchor is not unique for: {bug.name}")
+            try:
+                target.write_bytes(current.replace(bug.old, bug.new, 1))
+                outcome = run_test(bug.test)
+                caught = outcome.returncode != 0
+                results.append(f"{'CAUGHT' if caught else 'MISSED'} | {bug.test} | {bug.name}")
+                if not caught:
+                    results.append(outcome.stdout.strip() or "mutation test exited successfully")
+            finally:
+                target.write_bytes(clean)
+
+        caught_count = sum(row.startswith("CAUGHT") for row in results)
+        output = "\n".join([*results, f"{caught_count}/{len(BUGS)} caught"]) + "\n"
+        (HERE / "plant_bugs_3_output.txt").write_text(output, encoding="utf-8")
+        sys.stdout.write(output)
+        return 0 if caught_count == len(BUGS) else 1
+    finally:
+        for relative, original in clean_files.items():
+            target = ROOT / relative
+            target.write_bytes(original)
+            parked = BACKUP / (relative.replace("/", "__") + ".bak")
+            if parked.exists() and parked.read_bytes() != original:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"backup mismatch while restoring {relative}")
+            parked.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+        if BACKUP.exists() and not any(BACKUP.iterdir()):
+            BACKUP.rmdir()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+"""Hand-worked D1 edge-side cases derived from close-stamped H1 candles."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
+
+import pandas as pd
+import pytest
+
+from app.core.enums import Side, Timeframe
+from app.strategy.edge_side import edge_side
+
+
+def daily_context(closes: list[float], *, partial_close: float | None = None):
+    start = datetime(2026, 1, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
+    index = pd.date_range(start=start, periods=len(closes) * 24, freq="1h")
+    hourly_closes = [value for value in closes for _ in range(24)]
+    frame = pd.DataFrame({"close": hourly_closes}, index=index)
+    if partial_close is not None:
+        partial_index = pd.date_range(index[-1] + timedelta(hours=1), periods=23, freq="1h")
+        frame = pd.concat([frame, pd.DataFrame({"close": partial_close}, index=partial_index)])
+    at = pd.Timestamp(frame.index[-1])
+    return {Timeframe.H1: frame}, at
+
+
+def test_rising_daily_mean_with_close_above_it_is_buy():
+    # The last two 50-close means are 124.5 and 125.5; close 150 is above the rising mean.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.BUY
+
+
+def test_falling_daily_mean_with_close_below_it_is_sell():
+    # The last two 50-close means are 175.5 and 174.5; close 150 is below the falling mean.
+    frames, at = daily_context([200.0 - day for day in range(51)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.SELL
+
+
+def test_close_above_a_falling_mean_is_mixed():
+    # The current mean falls from 175.5 to 175.3, while close 190 stays above it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([200.0 - day for day in range(50)] + [190.0])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_close_below_a_rising_mean_is_mixed():
+    # The current mean rises from 124.5 to 124.9, while close 120 stays below it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)] + [120.0])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_exactly_fifty_closed_daily_bars_do_not_guess_the_mean_slope():
+    # Fifty closes form one 50-day mean, but there is no prior full-window mean to compare with it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_forty_nine_closed_daily_bars_return_no_side():
+    # Moving the cutoff back one day leaves exactly 49 complete daily bins from these 1,200 H1 rows.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)])
+    at -= pd.Timedelta(days=1)
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_unclosed_daily_bar_does_not_change_the_edge_side():
+    # The 51st full close is 150 with means 175.5 -> 174.5; a forming 500 close would reverse the regime.
+    closes = [200.0 - day for day in range(51)]
+    frames, at = daily_context(closes, partial_close=500.0)
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.SELL
+
+
+def test_entry_at_or_above_daily_raises_value_error():
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="smaller than D1"):
+        edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.D1)
+
+
+def test_short_h1_history_returns_no_side():
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    frame = frames[Timeframe.H1].drop(frames[Timeframe.H1].index[10:35])
+    frames = {Timeframe.H1: frame}
+    assert len(frame) < 1200
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None

+"""Hand-worked weighted-score cases; every expected score is calculated in the test comments."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+
+from app.strategy.weighing import Scale, Weight, score
+
+
+def test_all_readings_agree():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("a", 2.0, "true"), Weight("b", 1.0, "high")), 1.0)
+    got = score({"a": True, "b": 1.0}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 1.0  # (2 + 1) / (2 + 1)
+    assert got.supported == ["a", "b"]
+    assert got.opposed == [] and got.missing == [] and got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_all_readings_disagree():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("a", 2.0, "true"), Weight("b", 1.0, "high")), 0.5)
+    got = score({"a": False, "b": 0.0}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 0.0  # (0 + 0) / 3
+    assert got.supported == [] and got.opposed == ["a", "b"]
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_mixed_readings_use_weighted_contributions():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("yes", 2.0, "true"), Weight("trend", 3.0, "high")), 0.5)
+    got = score({"yes": True, "trend": 0.4}, scale)
+    assert got.score == pytest.approx(3.2 / 5.0)  # (2 + 3 * .4) / 5
+    assert got.supported == ["yes"] and got.opposed == ["trend"]
+    assert got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_missing_reading_is_removed_from_the_denominator():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("yes", 1.0, "true"), Weight("absent", 3.0, "true")), 0.9)
+    got = score({"yes": True}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 1.0  # 1 / 1, not 1 / 4
+    assert got.supported == ["yes"] and got.missing == ["absent"]
+    assert got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_low_numeric_reading_scores_the_complement():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("noise", 4.0, "low"),), 0.5)
+    got = score({"noise": 0.25}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 0.75  # 4 * (1 - .25) / 4
+    assert got.supported == ["noise"] and got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_empty_scale_scores_zero_and_has_no_readings():
+    got = score({}, Scale((), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0
+    assert got.supported == [] and got.opposed == [] and got.missing == []
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_zero_weight_is_readable_but_cannot_create_a_score():
+    got = score({"signal": True}, Scale((Weight("signal", 0.0, "true"),), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0
+    assert got.supported == ["signal"] and got.opposed == []
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_threshold_is_met_at_equality():
+    got = score({"signal": 0.75}, Scale((Weight("signal", 2.0, "high"),), 0.75))
+    assert got.score == 0.75  # (2 * .75) / 2
+    assert got.meets_threshold  # The documented comparison is >=.
+
+
+def test_none_is_reported_as_missing():
+    got = score({"signal": None}, Scale((Weight("signal", 1.0, "true"),), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0 and got.missing == ["signal"]
+    assert got.supported == [] and got.opposed == [] and not got.meets_threshold

+"""Derive the higher-timeframe edge side from completed daily closes."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+
+import pandas as pd
+
+from app.core.enums import Side, Timeframe
+
+
+def edge_side(
+    frames: Mapping[Timeframe, pd.DataFrame], at: pd.Timestamp, entry: Timeframe
+) -> Side | None:
+    """Return the D1 side above ``entry``; no clear D1 edge means no trade.
+
+    The lane's H1 index is close-stamped, so it is shifted to the bar open before UTC-day resampling.
+    Only completed daily bars are used. A rising 50-day simple mean needs two full windows (51 closes);
+    a shorter history or a mixed/flat regime returns ``None``. This is the owner's hard rule, not a
+    configurable fallback: no clear edge side above the entry frame means no trade.
+    """
+    if entry.seconds >= Timeframe.D1.seconds:
+        raise ValueError("entry timeframe must be smaller than D1")
+
+    h1 = frames.get(Timeframe.H1)
+    if h1 is None or len(h1) < 1200 or "close" not in h1:
+        return None
+
+    opens = h1.copy()
+    opens.index = pd.DatetimeIndex(opens.index) - pd.Timedelta(hours=1)
+    daily = opens.resample("1D").agg({"close": "last"}).dropna()
+    closed = daily[(daily.index + pd.Timedelta(days=1)) <= pd.Timestamp(at)]
+    if len(closed) < 51:
+        return None
+
+    means = closed.close.rolling(window=50, min_periods=50).mean()
+    current_close = float(closed.close.iloc[-1])
+    current_mean = float(means.iloc[-1])
+    previous_mean = float(means.iloc[-2])
+    if current_close > current_mean and current_mean > previous_mean:
+        return Side.BUY
+    if current_close < current_mean and current_mean < previous_mean:
+        return Side.SELL
+    return None

+"""A validated, inert vessel for research-supplied weighted trade readings."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Literal
+
+Wants = Literal["high", "low", "true", "false"]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Weight:
+    """A reading and the nonnegative amount it contributes to a weighted decision."""
+
+    name: str
+    weight: float
+    wants: Wants
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not self.name:
+            raise ValueError("weight name must not be empty")
+        if not math.isfinite(self.weight) or self.weight < 0:
+            raise ValueError("weight must be finite and >= 0")
+        if self.wants not in ("high", "low", "true", "false"):
+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported wants value: {self.wants!r}")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Scale:
+    """The readings and minimum normalized score required to qualify."""
+
+    weights: tuple[Weight, ...]
+    threshold: float
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not math.isfinite(self.threshold) or not 0 <= self.threshold <= 1:
+            raise ValueError("threshold must be finite and in [0, 1]")
+        names = [reading.name for reading in self.weights]
+        if len(names) != len(set(names)):
+            raise ValueError("weight names must be unique")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ScoreResult:
+    """Normalized score, per-reading classifications, and threshold outcome."""
+
+    score: float
+    supported: list[str]
+    opposed: list[str]
+    missing: list[str]
+    meets_threshold: bool
+
+
+def score(readings: Mapping[str, float | bool | None], scale: Scale) -> ScoreResult:
+    """Score available readings over their readable weight only.
+
+    Numeric values must already be normalized to ``[0, 1]`` by the caller. ``high`` earns
+    ``weight * value`` and ``low`` earns ``weight * (1 - value)``; a numeric reading supports when
+    its contribution is at least half its weight, otherwise it opposes. Boolean readings earn full
+    weight only when their value matches ``true`` or ``false``. Missing values are excluded from
+    both numerator and denominator. The threshold is met at ``score >= threshold``; an empty or
+    zero-readable-weight scale cannot meet it.
+    """
+    numerator = 0.0
+    denominator = 0.0
+    supported: list[str] = []
+    opposed: list[str] = []
+    missing: list[str] = []
+
+    for item in scale.weights:
+        value = readings.get(item.name)
+        if value is None:
+            missing.append(item.name)
+            continue
+
+        if isinstance(value, bool):
+            if item.wants not in ("true", "false"):
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: boolean reading requires wants='true' or 'false'")
+            agrees = value is (item.wants == "true")
+            contribution = item.weight if agrees else 0.0
+            if agrees:
+                supported.append(item.name)
+            else:
+                opposed.append(item.name)
+        else:
+            if item.wants not in ("high", "low"):
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: numeric reading requires wants='high' or 'low'")
+            numeric = float(value)
+            if not math.isfinite(numeric) or not 0 <= numeric <= 1:
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: numeric reading must be finite and in [0, 1]")
+            fraction = numeric if item.wants == "high" else 1.0 - numeric
+            contribution = item.weight * fraction
+            (supported if fraction >= 0.5 else opposed).append(item.name)
+        numerator += contribution
+        denominator += item.weight
+
+    total = numerator / denominator if denominator > 0 else 0.0
+    meets = denominator > 0 and total >= scale.threshold
+    return ScoreResult(total, supported, opposed, missing, meets)

+# DEV_NOTES_3
+
+Date: 2026-10-27
+
+## Tasks A–C
+
+- **A — `edge_side.py`:** Added a pure D1 regime reader from close-stamped H1 candles. It shifts the index back one hour, resamples daily closes, filters daily bars closed at `at`, and returns BUY/SELL only when close and the 50-day SMA slope agree. It rejects entry frames at or above D1 and returns `None` for missing/short data, mixed readings, and an incomplete D1 bar.
+- **B — trend and range bots:** Added `require_edge_side=False` to both parameter models. The trend bots check it immediately after their session window and before reading other decision data; enabling it requests 1,200 H1 warmup bars. The range bot checks the break side against the D1 side after finding a break. A missing edge side holds every enabled bot with `AGAINST_EDGE_SIDE`. Default behavior remains off. The shared API sample fixture now records the two new `false` defaults.
+- **C — `weighing.py`:** Added immutable `Weight` and `Scale` models and `score()`. Missing readings leave both parts of the ratio; numeric inputs are validated in `[0, 1]` and are not normalized by this module. The normalized score is weighted contribution / available weight. Boolean support means the value matches `wants`; numeric support means the contribution fraction is at least 0.5. `meets_threshold` uses `>=`; empty and zero-readable-weight scales do not meet even a zero threshold. No strategy calls the scorer yet.
+
+## Tests and mutation proof
+
+There are 26 new test cases. Each case was run against a targeted one-line production mutation; the default-off test has separate mutations for the trend and range parameter defaults. The 25 planted mutations caught all 25 cases. Full details are in [plant_bugs_3_output.txt](plant_bugs_3_output.txt).

+
+## Clarity and interpretation
+
+No direct contradiction appeared within the detailed Task A–C requirements. Three scope details needed explicit treatment:
+
+1. Exactly 50 closed daily closes produce one 50-day mean, but cannot establish whether that mean is rising or falling without a prior full 50-day window. I fail closed with `None` at 50 and classify only once 51 closes are available. This is covered by the 50-bar and 49-bar boundary tests.
+2. The spec asks for supported/opposed lists for continuous numeric readings but does not define their dividing line. I classify the normalized contribution fraction at or above 0.5 as support and below 0.5 as opposition, documented in `score()`.
+3. The owner’s rule says it applies to the AI trader too, while Task B specifies only `trend_box_down`, `trend_box_up`, and `range_break`, with a new opt-in parameter on those classes. I applied Task B to its three named strategies and did not add an AI-trader gate because no AI parameter or gate ordering is specified. The AI path therefore remains outside this implementation and needs an explicit follow-up decision to fulfill the wider statement.
+

+- Full suite after API sample update: **3,974 passed, 9 skipped**, 3 existing warnings, 20m50s.

It calls `load_settings()` with the default `.env` path, so it likely read `.env` once before I stopped it; I did not inspect, display, or modify the file. The completed parity replay used a config-only wrapper instead. This was my mistake, and it is recorded here explicitly.

+def restore_any() -> None:
+    """Recover any source files parked before an interrupted mutation run."""
+    if not BACKUP.exists():
+        return
+    for parked in sorted(BACKUP.glob("*.bak")):
+        relative = parked.stem.replace("__", "/")
+        (ROOT / relative).write_bytes(parked.read_bytes())
+        parked.unlink()
+        sys.stdout.write(f"restored {relative} from an interrupted run\n")
+    if not any(BACKUP.iterdir()):
+        BACKUP.rmdir()
+
+
+def run_test(test: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
+    return subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed interpreter and repository-owned test selectors
+        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", f"tests/unit/{test}"],
+        cwd=ROOT,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=False,
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    restore_any()
+    test_paths = sorted({bug.test.split("::", 1)[0] for bug in BUGS})
+    baseline = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed interpreter and repository-owned test paths
+        [
+            sys.executable,
+            "-m",
+            "pytest",
+            "-q",
+            "-p",
+            "no:cacheprovider",
+            *[f"tests/unit/{p}" for p in test_paths],
+        ],
+        cwd=ROOT,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=False,
+    )
+    if baseline.returncode:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"focused baseline tests failed:\n{baseline.stdout}\n{baseline.stderr}")
+
+    BACKUP.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    clean_files: dict[str, bytes] = {}
+    results: list[str] = []
+    try:
+        for bug in BUGS:
+            target = ROOT / bug.path
+            clean = clean_files.setdefault(bug.path, target.read_bytes())
+            parked = BACKUP / (bug.path.replace("/", "__") + ".bak")
+            if not parked.exists():
+                parked.write_bytes(clean)
+            current = target.read_bytes()
+            if current.count(bug.old) != 1 or bug.old == bug.new:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"mutation anchor is not unique for: {bug.name}")
+            try:
+                target.write_bytes(current.replace(bug.old, bug.new, 1))
+                outcome = run_test(bug.test)
+                caught = outcome.returncode != 0
+                results.append(f"{'CAUGHT' if caught else 'MISSED'} | {bug.test} | {bug.name}")
+                if not caught:
+                    results.append(outcome.stdout.strip() or "mutation test exited successfully")
+            finally:
+                target.write_bytes(clean)
+
+        caught_count = sum(row.startswith("CAUGHT") for row in results)
+        output = "\n".join([*results, f"{caught_count}/{len(BUGS)} caught"]) + "\n"
+        (HERE / "plant_bugs_3_output.txt").write_text(output, encoding="utf-8")
+        sys.stdout.write(output)
+        return 0 if caught_count == len(BUGS) else 1
+    finally:
+        for relative, original in clean_files.items():
+            target = ROOT / relative
+            target.write_bytes(original)
+            parked = BACKUP / (relative.replace("/", "__") + ".bak")
+            if parked.exists() and parked.read_bytes() != original:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"backup mismatch while restoring {relative}")
+            parked.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+        if BACKUP.exists() and not any(BACKUP.iterdir()):
+            BACKUP.rmdir()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+"""Hand-worked D1 edge-side cases derived from close-stamped H1 candles."""

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
+
+import pandas as pd
+import pytest

+from app.core.enums import Side, Timeframe
+from app.strategy.edge_side import edge_side
+
+
+def daily_context(closes: list[float], *, partial_close: float | None = None):
+    start = datetime(2026, 1, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
+    index = pd.date_range(start=start, periods=len(closes) * 24, freq="1h")
+    hourly_closes = [value for value in closes for _ in range(24)]
+    frame = pd.DataFrame({"close": hourly_closes}, index=index)
+    if partial_close is not None:
+        partial_index = pd.date_range(index[-1] + timedelta(hours=1), periods=23, freq="1h")
+        frame = pd.concat([frame, pd.DataFrame({"close": partial_close}, index=partial_index)])
+    at = pd.Timestamp(frame.index[-1])
+    return {Timeframe.H1: frame}, at
+
+
+def test_rising_daily_mean_with_close_above_it_is_buy():
+    # The last two 50-close means are 124.5 and 125.5; close 150 is above the rising mean.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.BUY
+
+
+def test_falling_daily_mean_with_close_below_it_is_sell():
+    # The last two 50-close means are 175.5 and 174.5; close 150 is below the falling mean.
+    frames, at = daily_context([200.0 - day for day in range(51)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.SELL
+
+
+def test_close_above_a_falling_mean_is_mixed():
+    # The current mean falls from 175.5 to 175.3, while close 190 stays above it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([200.0 - day for day in range(50)] + [190.0])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_close_below_a_rising_mean_is_mixed():
+    # The current mean rises from 124.5 to 124.9, while close 120 stays below it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)] + [120.0])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_exactly_fifty_closed_daily_bars_do_not_guess_the_mean_slope():
+    # Fifty closes form one 50-day mean, but there is no prior full-window mean to compare with it.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)])
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_forty_nine_closed_daily_bars_return_no_side():
+    # Moving the cutoff back one day leaves exactly 49 complete daily bins from these 1,200 H1 rows.
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(50)])
+    at -= pd.Timedelta(days=1)
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None
+
+
+def test_unclosed_daily_bar_does_not_change_the_edge_side():
+    # The 51st full close is 150 with means 175.5 -> 174.5; a forming 500 close would reverse the regime.
+    closes = [200.0 - day for day in range(51)]
+    frames, at = daily_context(closes, partial_close=500.0)
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is Side.SELL
+
+
+def test_entry_at_or_above_daily_raises_value_error():
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="smaller than D1"):
+        edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.D1)
+
+
+def test_short_h1_history_returns_no_side():
+    frames, at = daily_context([100.0 + day for day in range(51)])
+    frame = frames[Timeframe.H1].drop(frames[Timeframe.H1].index[10:35])
+    frames = {Timeframe.H1: frame}
+    assert len(frame) < 1200
+    assert edge_side(frames, at, Timeframe.M5) is None

+"""Hand-worked weighted-score cases; every expected score is calculated in the test comments."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+
+from app.strategy.weighing import Scale, Weight, score
+
+
+def test_all_readings_agree():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("a", 2.0, "true"), Weight("b", 1.0, "high")), 1.0)
+    got = score({"a": True, "b": 1.0}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 1.0  # (2 + 1) / (2 + 1)
+    assert got.supported == ["a", "b"]
+    assert got.opposed == [] and got.missing == [] and got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_all_readings_disagree():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("a", 2.0, "true"), Weight("b", 1.0, "high")), 0.5)
+    got = score({"a": False, "b": 0.0}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 0.0  # (0 + 0) / 3
+    assert got.supported == [] and got.opposed == ["a", "b"]
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_mixed_readings_use_weighted_contributions():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("yes", 2.0, "true"), Weight("trend", 3.0, "high")), 0.5)
+    got = score({"yes": True, "trend": 0.4}, scale)
+    assert got.score == pytest.approx(3.2 / 5.0)  # (2 + 3 * .4) / 5
+    assert got.supported == ["yes"] and got.opposed == ["trend"]
+    assert got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_missing_reading_is_removed_from_the_denominator():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("yes", 1.0, "true"), Weight("absent", 3.0, "true")), 0.9)
+    got = score({"yes": True}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 1.0  # 1 / 1, not 1 / 4
+    assert got.supported == ["yes"] and got.missing == ["absent"]
+    assert got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_low_numeric_reading_scores_the_complement():
+    scale = Scale((Weight("noise", 4.0, "low"),), 0.5)
+    got = score({"noise": 0.25}, scale)
+    assert got.score == 0.75  # 4 * (1 - .25) / 4
+    assert got.supported == ["noise"] and got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_empty_scale_scores_zero_and_has_no_readings():
+    got = score({}, Scale((), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0
+    assert got.supported == [] and got.opposed == [] and got.missing == []
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_zero_weight_is_readable_but_cannot_create_a_score():
+    got = score({"signal": True}, Scale((Weight("signal", 0.0, "true"),), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0
+    assert got.supported == ["signal"] and got.opposed == []
+    assert not got.meets_threshold
+
+
+def test_threshold_is_met_at_equality():
+    got = score({"signal": 0.75}, Scale((Weight("signal", 2.0, "high"),), 0.75))
+    assert got.score == 0.75  # (2 * .75) / 2
+    assert got.meets_threshold  # The documented comparison is >=.
+
+
+def test_none_is_reported_as_missing():
+    got = score({"signal": None}, Scale((Weight("signal", 1.0, "true"),), 0.0))
+    assert got.score == 0.0 and got.missing == ["signal"]
+    assert got.supported == [] and got.opposed == [] and not got.meets_threshold

# DEV_NOTES_3

Date: 2026-10-27

## Tasks Aâ€“C

- **A â€” `edge_side.py`:** Added a pure D1 regime reader from close-stamped H1 candles. It shifts the index back one hour, resamples daily closes, filters daily bars closed at `at`, and returns BUY/SELL only when close and the 50-day SMA slope agree. It rejects entry frames at or above D1 and returns `None` for missing/short data, mixed readings, and an incomplete D1 bar.
- **B â€” trend and range bots:** Added `require_edge_side=False` to both parameter models. The trend bots check it immediately after their session window and before reading other decision data; enabling it requests 1,200 H1 warmup bars. The range bot checks the break side against the D1 side after finding a break. A missing edge side holds every enabled bot with `AGAINST_EDGE_SIDE`. Default behavior remains off. The shared API sample fixture now records the two new `false` defaults.
- **C â€” `weighing.py`:** Added immutable `Weight` and `Scale` models and `score()`. Missing readings leave both parts of the ratio; numeric inputs are validated in `[0, 1]` and are not normalized by this module. The normalized score is weighted contribution / available weight. Boolean support means the value matches `wants`; numeric support means the contribution fraction is at least 0.5. `meets_threshold` uses `>=`; empty and zero-readable-weight scales do not meet even a zero threshold. No strategy calls the scorer yet.

## Tests and mutation proof

There are 26 new test cases. Each case was run against a targeted one-line production mutation; the default-off test has separate mutations for the trend and range parameter defaults. The 25 planted mutations caught all 25 cases. Full details are in [plant_bugs_3_output.txt](plant_bugs_3_output.txt).

| Test | Mutation used | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `edge_side`: rising mean + close above | Reverse the rising-SMA comparison | CAUGHT |
| `edge_side`: falling mean + close below | Reverse the falling-SMA comparison | CAUGHT |
| `edge_side`: close above falling mean | Ignore the SMA slope in the BUY condition | CAUGHT |
| `edge_side`: close below rising mean | Ignore the SMA slope in the SELL condition | CAUGHT |
| `edge_side`: exactly 50 closed D1 bars | Return BUY when only one full 50-day mean exists | CAUGHT |

+"""Derive the higher-timeframe edge side from completed daily closes."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+
+import pandas as pd
+
+from app.core.enums import Side, Timeframe
+
+
+def edge_side(
+    frames: Mapping[Timeframe, pd.DataFrame], at: pd.Timestamp, entry: Timeframe
+) -> Side | None:
+    """Return the D1 side above ``entry``; no clear D1 edge means no trade.
+
+    The lane's H1 index is close-stamped, so it is shifted to the bar open before UTC-day resampling.
+    Only completed daily bars are used. A rising 50-day simple mean needs two full windows (51 closes);
+    a shorter history or a mixed/flat regime returns ``None``. This is the owner's hard rule, not a
+    configurable fallback: no clear edge side above the entry frame means no trade.
+    """
+    if entry.seconds >= Timeframe.D1.seconds:
+        raise ValueError("entry timeframe must be smaller than D1")
+
+    h1 = frames.get(Timeframe.H1)
+    if h1 is None or len(h1) < 1200 or "close" not in h1:
+        return None
+
+    opens = h1.copy()
+    opens.index = pd.DatetimeIndex(opens.index) - pd.Timedelta(hours=1)
+    daily = opens.resample("1D").agg({"close": "last"}).dropna()
+    closed = daily[(daily.index + pd.Timedelta(days=1)) <= pd.Timestamp(at)]
+    if len(closed) < 51:
+        return None
+
+    means = closed.close.rolling(window=50, min_periods=50).mean()
+    current_close = float(closed.close.iloc[-1])
+    current_mean = float(means.iloc[-1])
+    previous_mean = float(means.iloc[-2])
+    if current_close > current_mean and current_mean > previous_mean:
+        return Side.BUY
+    if current_close < current_mean and current_mean < previous_mean:
+        return Side.SELL
+    return None

+"""A validated, inert vessel for research-supplied weighted trade readings."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Literal
+
+Wants = Literal["high", "low", "true", "false"]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Weight:
+    """A reading and the nonnegative amount it contributes to a weighted decision."""
+
+    name: str
+    weight: float
+    wants: Wants
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not self.name:
+            raise ValueError("weight name must not be empty")
+        if not math.isfinite(self.weight) or self.weight < 0:
+            raise ValueError("weight must be finite and >= 0")
+        if self.wants not in ("high", "low", "true", "false"):
+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported wants value: {self.wants!r}")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Scale:
+    """The readings and minimum normalized score required to qualify."""
+
+    weights: tuple[Weight, ...]
+    threshold: float
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not math.isfinite(self.threshold) or not 0 <= self.threshold <= 1:
+            raise ValueError("threshold must be finite and in [0, 1]")
+        names = [reading.name for reading in self.weights]
+        if len(names) != len(set(names)):
+            raise ValueError("weight names must be unique")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ScoreResult:
+    """Normalized score, per-reading classifications, and threshold outcome."""
+
+    score: float
+    supported: list[str]
+    opposed: list[str]
+    missing: list[str]
+    meets_threshold: bool
+
+
+def score(readings: Mapping[str, float | bool | None], scale: Scale) -> ScoreResult:
+    """Score available readings over their readable weight only.
+
+    Numeric values must already be normalized to ``[0, 1]`` by the caller. ``high`` earns
+    ``weight * value`` and ``low`` earns ``weight * (1 - value)``; a numeric reading supports when
+    its contribution is at least half its weight, otherwise it opposes. Boolean readings earn full
+    weight only when their value matches ``true`` or ``false``. Missing values are excluded from
+    both numerator and denominator. The threshold is met at ``score >= threshold``; an empty or
+    zero-readable-weight scale cannot meet it.
+    """
+    numerator = 0.0
+    denominator = 0.0
+    supported: list[str] = []
+    opposed: list[str] = []
+    missing: list[str] = []
+
+    for item in scale.weights:
+        value = readings.get(item.name)
+        if value is None:
+            missing.append(item.name)
+            continue
+
+        if isinstance(value, bool):
+            if item.wants not in ("true", "false"):
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: boolean reading requires wants='true' or 'false'")
+            agrees = value is (item.wants == "true")
+            contribution = item.weight if agrees else 0.0
+            if agrees:
+                supported.append(item.name)
+            else:
+                opposed.append(item.name)
+        else:
+            if item.wants not in ("high", "low"):
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: numeric reading requires wants='high' or 'low'")
+            numeric = float(value)
+            if not math.isfinite(numeric) or not 0 <= numeric <= 1:
+                raise ValueError(f"{item.name}: numeric reading must be finite and in [0, 1]")
+            fraction = numeric if item.wants == "high" else 1.0 - numeric
+            contribution = item.weight * fraction
+            (supported if fraction >= 0.5 else opposed).append(item.name)
+        numerator += contribution
+        denominator += item.weight
+
+    total = numerator / denominator if denominator > 0 else 0.0
+    meets = denominator > 0 and total >= scale.threshold
+    return ScoreResult(total, supported, opposed, missing, meets)
